quizzes.title: 15.1 Module 15 Introduction: Fascism and the Slump
quizzes.description:
MODULE INTRODUCTION
Module Introduction: Fascism and the Slump
Survey · 2 questions · not graded
■ ─ ■ ─ ■
Before you start

Welcome to Fascism and the Slump. Answer the questions below before you open the first lesson. Your answers help your teacher see where the class is starting. This survey is not graded.

This module's goals:
  • Explain how Mussolini came to power and what fascism claimed to be.
  • Describe how hyperinflation and the Depression damaged the Weimar Republic.
  • Compare how Germany and the United States responded to the Depression.

questions.text: Before you read: Why did some democracies bend in the Depression and others break? Give your first answer in two or three sentences. You will answer it again at the end of the module, so it is fine if your answer changes.
I have read this module's goals and I know what I am working toward this week.

answers.text: Yes, I have read them
Not yet, I will read them before the first lesson

quizzes.title: 15.7 Reading Quiz: Fascism and the Slump
quizzes.description:
READING QUIZ
Reading Quiz: Fascism and the Slump
7 questions · 7 points
■ ─ ■ ─ ■
Before you start

This quiz covers both lessons and both primary sources for this module. It has 7 questions. Most ask you to work something out from what you read, not to find a sentence in the text. You may look back at the lessons and sources while you work.

HOW TO WORK
Read the two lessons and the two primary sources first, and keep your notes in My Notebook. Then answer the questions below.

questions.text: Italy’s army in Rome was larger and better armed than the Blackshirts in October 1922. Why did the March on Rome still succeed?

answers.text: The army joined the Fascists on the road to Rome
King Victor Emmanuel refused to sign a martial law decree and invited Mussolini to form a government
Parliament voted to give Mussolini emergency powers
The prime minister resigned and the army went home

questions.text: Why did many property owners and middle-class Italians tolerate the violence of the Blackshirt squads?

answers.text: They believed the squads were an official branch of the army
They agreed with the squads that Italy should leave the Allies
They had been promised that the King would be removed
They feared a Bolshevik revolution and wanted an order that parliament could not supply

questions.text: According to “The Doctrine of Fascism,” how should the individual relate to the state?

answers.text: The individual counts only as far as his interests coincide with those of the state
The individual’s rights come first, and the state exists to protect them
The individual and the state should stay separate and leave each other alone
The individual should serve the state only in wartime

questions.text: Why did the hyperinflation of 1923 weaken many Germans’ loyalty to the Weimar Republic?

answers.text: It made Germany richer than France, so Germans stopped needing the republic
It ended the reparations payments, so Germans no longer feared the Allies
It wiped out the savings of middle-class families, who felt that the republic and the whole system of money and law had betrayed them
It forced the Kaiser to return from exile

questions.text: Germany’s republic broke in the Depression, and America’s bent. Which difference does “Inflation, Crash, and Two Answers: Weimar and Roosevelt's America” give?

answers.text: America had avoided bank failures, and Germany had not
America’s institutions were older and its people had long habits of self-government, while Germany’s republic was young and many Germans never felt loyal to it
Germany refused help from American banks, and America accepted it
Germany had a king, and America did not

questions.text: Which statement best compares Roosevelt’s first inaugural address with Mussolini’s “Doctrine of Fascism”?

answers.text: Both say the leader may ignore the legislature in a crisis
Both say that individuals should be free of the state in peacetime
Both say that war is the highest test of a nation
Roosevelt says he will first act within the Constitution and with Congress, while Mussolini says nothing of value can exist outside the state

questions.text: “Inflation, Crash, and Two Answers: Weimar and Roosevelt's America” notes that Stresemann died three weeks before the Wall Street crash, and says his death came at the worst moment. What is the lesson suggesting?

answers.text: The choices of individual leaders and the timing of events mattered, so Germany’s fate was not fixed in advance
Stresemann’s policies had caused the crash
Germany’s democracy could not have survived under any leader
The crash would not have happened if he had lived

discussions.title: 15.8 Discussion: Why did some democracies bend in the Depression and others break?
discussions.html:
DISCUSSION
Why did some democracies bend in the Depression and others break?
Habits, institutions, and the choices of a few leaders.
Graded discussion · 10 points · one post and one reply
■ ─ ■ ─ ■
HOW TO WORK
Read the two lessons and the two primary sources first, and look over your notes in My Notebook. Then post your answer to the prompt below, and reply to one classmate.
DISCUSSION PROMPT

This week’s question: Why did some democracies bend in the Depression and others break?

Pick one democracy that bent and one that broke. Name two causes of the difference, and say which cause you think mattered most.

Write 150 to 250 words. State one claim you believe is true. Then explain why, using the specific evidence named above. Keep to what the lessons and the sources show. If you are guessing, say so.

Then add one sentence on self-government. Name one habit or decision from the lessons that kept a democracy standing, or let it fall. Say why it mattered.

RESPOND TO A CLASSMATE

Reply to one classmate. Do you agree with their reasoning? If so, strengthen it with a fact or decision they did not use. If not, say politely where you think it falls short, and give your reason.

GRADING RUBRIC (10 pts)
CriteriaSubstantive (full credit)Thin (partial credit)Missing (no credit)
Your claim and your reasons
6 pts		Takes a clear side, uses the specific evidence the prompt asks for, and explains why it supports the claim.Takes a side but gives general reasons, or leaves out part of what the prompt asks for.No post, or no claim.
Your reply to a classmate
4 pts		Answers one classmate's actual reasoning. Strengthens it or says where it falls short, politely and with a reason.Replies, but only to agree or disagree with no reason.No reply.
10 pts total
